summary: The University of Florida and Nvidia Corp. are partnering to build what they claim will be the fastest artificial intelligence supercomputer in academia. summary: Intel announced a significant delay in the rollout of its 7nm CPUs, pushing their debut to late 2022 or early 2023. This delay is attributed to a "defect mode" causing yield degradation, putting Intel approximately twelve months behind its internal targets for 7nm process. The company is now exploring contingency plans, including the use of third-party foundries for some components and entire chip designs, and plans to increase shipments of 10nm chips by 20%.

title: Banking on AI: RBC Builds a DGX-Powered Private Cloud
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) has built an NVIDIA DGX-powered private cloud to enhance its AI capabilities and transform client experiences, leveraging a strategic investment in AI through its research institute, Borealis AI. This new infrastructure allows RBC to run thousands of simulations and analyze millions of data points rapidly, enabling the development of smart applications and significant savings in total cost of ownership. summary: Hermann Hauser, co-founder of ARM, stated that a potential sale of the British chip designer to US firm Nvidia would be "disastrous." He argues that Nvidia, being a competitor to many of ARM's licensees, would compromise ARM's crucial neutrality, leading current licensees to seek alternatives. This system is crucial for triaging COVID-19 patients by providing near-instant evaluations. The company has partnered with GE Healthcare and utilizes NVIDIA technology to commercialize its AI solutions, aiming to enhance medical diagnosis and treatment efficiency.

summary: Atomwise, a drug discovery startup, has successfully raised $123 million, bringing its total capital to nearly $175 million. The funding will be used to scale its AI platform, develop its internal drug pipeline, and expand partnerships with companies like Eli Lilly and Bayer. Atomwise's AtomNet model utilizes a convolutional neural network to rapidly screen billions of compounds, significantly accelerating the small molecule drug discovery process with the help of NVIDIA GPUs.

summary: Blaize, an AI chip startup, is launching its Xplorer Accelerator cards and Pathfinder P1600 embedded modules to compete with Intel and Nvidia. summary: Nvidia reported better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings, with overall revenue up 50% year-over-year. CEO Jensen Huang anticipates a strong second half for gaming, despite declines in professional visualization and automotive segments due to the pandemic.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: Our Future Is About ‘Data Center-Scale Computing’
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized that the company's future hinges on "data center-scale computing" rather than just chip-level optimization. This strategy is highlighted by the recent acquisition of Mellanox and the success of its data center division, which for the first time surpassed gaming revenue. summary: Nvidia reported record sales for its latest quarter, driven by strong demand for online gaming and remote computing services during the pandemic. This platform is trained to detect and label almost any object, accelerating the training process by up to 50x compared to human annotation. V7 Darwin is optimized on NVIDIA GPUs and is being applied across various industries, including healthcare, manufacturing, and agriculture, to improve efficiency and reduce costs associated with AI model development.

This series, based on Nvidia's Ampere architecture, promises a significant generational leap in performance and power efficiency.

title: NVIDIA Delivers Greatest-Ever Generational Leap with GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs
summary: NVIDIA has unveiled its GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs, powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, delivering the most significant generational performance leap in GeForce history with up to 2x the performance and 1.9x the power efficiency of the previous generation. The company is, however, exploring building a plant in Arizona to mitigate some of these risks.

title: Micron Announces GDDR6X Memory, Powering the World's Fastest Graphics Cards
summary: Micron Technology announced GDDR6X, the world's fastest discrete graphics memory solution, capable of reaching system bandwidths up to 1 terabyte per second. This new memory, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, powers the new NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 and GeForce RTX 3080 GPUs, enabling advanced gaming experiences with high resolutions and real-time ray tracing. GDDR6X achieves its speed through innovative four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) signaling, significantly increasing memory bandwidth and offering lower power consumption per transaction.

title: ‘Fortnite’ Is RTX On! Real-Time Ray Tracing Comes to One of Most Popular Games on the Planet
summary: NVIDIA and Epic Games announced that Fortnite is integrating real-time ray tracing, AI-powered NVIDIA DLSS, and NVIDIA Reflex technology, significantly enhancing the game's visuals and responsiveness. The collaboration highlights how NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 Series GPUs are improving competitive gaming with next-level graphics and performance.

title: Micron Unveils GDDR6X Memory For NVIDIA GeForce RTX 30 Series – The Next Chapter In Graphics Memory
summary: Micron has introduced its new GDDR6X memory, designed for NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 30 series graphics cards, specifically the RTX 3090 and RTX 3080. This memory features PAM4 multi-level signaling, doubling the I/O data rate and achieving bandwidths up to 1 TB/s for high-fidelity gaming. GDDR6X also offers improved power efficiency, consuming 15% less power per transferred bit compared to GDDR6, and is expected to reach speeds higher than 21 Gbps in the future.

summary: An ERISA lawsuit has been filed against Nvidia over its 401(k) plan, with plaintiffs alleging excessive investment management fees and a failure to opt for lower-cost share classes. The robot is designed to provide a physical presence for remote employees in offices, facilitating better interaction and communication, and has seen increased interest due to COVID-19 for contact-free work and international business travel alternatives.

title: NVIDIA and Arm to Create World-Class AI Research Center in Cambridge
summary: NVIDIA and Arm are collaborating to establish a world-class AI research center in Cambridge, UK, which will serve as a hub for AI researchers, scientists, and startups globally. The initiative aims to propel the UK to global AI leadership and foster collaboration in crucial fields like healthcare, autonomous vehicles, and robotics.

NVIDIA plans to expand Arm’s R&D presence in Cambridge, UK, establish a world-class AI research and education center, and build an Arm/NVIDIA-powered AI supercomputer, all while maintaining Arm’s open-licensing model and customer neutrality.

summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Holdings from SoftBank is poised to significantly impact the global semiconductor industry, further solidifying Nvidia's position. title: Nvidia Confident U.S.-China Tech War Won’t Stop It From Buying Arm
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence in obtaining regulatory approvals for its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd., despite escalating U.S.-China tech tensions. The deal faces skepticism from Chinese experts and opposition from Arm co-founder Hermann Hauser, who warns of potential job losses and compromised business neutrality. Despite these challenges, Nvidia remains optimistic, citing past regulatory successes.

title: Fidelity U.S. Multifactor ETF Holdings
summary: This article details the holdings of the Fidelity U.S. Multifactor ETF (FLRG), which was established on September 15, 2020. The ETF focuses on total market equity, comprising 102 holdings and managing $286.35 million in assets under management. It tracks large-cap US stocks selected based on value, quality, low volatility, and momentum factors, with top holdings including NVIDIA Corp, Apple Inc, and Alphabet Inc.

title: NVIDIA Ampere Architecture Whitepaper Available Now
summary: NVIDIA has released a new whitepaper detailing its Ampere GA102 GPU Architecture, which powers the GeForce RTX 30 Series graphics cards. This comprehensive document provides an in-depth look at the architectural details of their latest GPUs, offering record-breaking performance for PC gamers. Further updates on GeForce GPU performance and features will be shared on GeForce.com.

title: Chip industry wants $50 billion to keep manufacturing in US
summary: The U.S. chip industry is requesting between $20 billion and $50 billion in federal incentives to prevent further manufacturing migration overseas, as other countries, particularly China, heavily invest in semiconductor production. The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) warns that without this investment, the U.S. risks losing its leadership in the sector and jeopardizing national security by relying on foreign supply chains for vital components. The move comes amid increased awareness in Washington regarding supply chain vulnerabilities due to the China-U.S. trade war and the pandemic.

title: A brewing U.S.-China tech cold war rattles the semiconductor industry
summary: The U.S. semiconductor industry is concerned about a brewing tech cold war with China, fearing disruptions to the global supply chain as trade tensions escalate. Companies are developing strategies like hoarding supplies or relocating production, while the U.S. government is pushing for domestic manufacturing incentives through legislation like the CHIPS for America Act and the American Foundries Act. This push aims to strengthen U.S. leadership in advanced technologies and reduce reliance on foreign chip production.

title: The biggest semiconductor deal in history should have been even bigger
summary: Nvidia's acquisition of Arm Holdings for $40 billion marks the semiconductor industry's largest deal, yet Arm's valuation is considered surprisingly low, lagging SoftBank's investment goals. Analysts believe Nvidia's ownership could help Arm realize its full potential, providing resources to a company whose technology is integral to various processors. The deal also highlights Europe's struggle to retain its tech giants, with many being acquired by US companies, though some European firms are now achieving significant market capitalization.

title: MPs to debate Arm Holdings $40bn sale despite Nvidia boss's guarantees
summary: MPs are set to debate the controversial $40bn sale of UK tech firm Arm Holdings to US-based Nvidia, despite Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang offering legally binding guarantees regarding jobs and investment in the UK. Concerns remain among politicians and Arm's co-founder about the potential impact on British interests and the company's neutrality, particularly regarding US legislation. The debate in Parliament aims to press the government for clarity on their stance and actions to safeguard Arm's future.

title: Moore’s Law Is Dead. Long Live Huang’s Law.
summary: This article discusses the decline of Moore's Law and introduces "Huang's Law," named after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang's Law describes the rapid advancement in specialized computing power, particularly for AI applications, driven by GPUs outpacing general-purpose CPUs. The article argues that specialized hardware will be crucial for developing true AI, even as Moore's Law, which predicted the doubling of computing power every 18 months, has reached its limits.

title: Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) To Equip Its Vehicles With NVIDIA’s Orin SoC Chipset To Facilitate Autonomous Driving Under a New Partnership Agreement
summary: Li Auto (NASDAQ: LI) has formed a partnership with NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Huizhou Desay SV Automotive to integrate NVIDIA's Orin SoC chipset into its upcoming smart SUV, expected in 2022. This collaboration positions Li Auto to independently develop L4 autonomous driving systems, leveraging Orin's powerful computing capabilities. The move highlights Li Auto's strategic focus on advanced autonomous technology for its Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREVs), which are gaining traction in China.

title: Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Global X Nasdaq 100 Covered Call & Growth ETF (QYLG), including its current price, performance metrics, expenses, and holdings. It also contrasts QYLG with other ETFs in similar categories based on factors like expense ratio, assets under management, and year-to-date returns. The report offers an in-depth analysis of the ETF's concentration, valuation, dividend, fund flows, and ESG scores, giving a comprehensive overview for potential investors.

title: Arm CTO on company's small, but vital Silicon Valley presence
summary: Arm Limited's CTO, Dipesh Patel, discussed the company's significant presence in Silicon Valley, despite its smaller size compared to its Cambridge, England office. Arm, which employs around 350 people in San Jose, is set to be acquired by Nvidia Corp. The article highlights the historical roots of Arm's Silicon Valley operations dating back to the mid-1990s.

title: There's No Such Thing as 'Huang's Law,' Despite Nvidia's AI Lead
summary: This article disputes the notion of "Huang's Law," which posits that AI silicon performance doubles every two years, similar to Moore's Law. The author argues that this "law" is a misinterpretation that conflates Moore's Law (transistor density) and Dennard scaling (performance per watt), and that Nvidia's AI advancements are heavily reliant on Moore's Law and other technological improvements, not an independent phenomenon. Furthermore, it is too early to declare such a law, and the rate of AI/ML improvement may not be sustainable.

title: Nvidia's ARM acquisition prompts Ceva upgrade
summary: Northland Capital Markets upgraded semiconductor IP company Ceva to "Outperform" and raised its price target to $48, citing Nvidia's ARM acquisition. Analyst Gus Richard highlights Ceva's strong IP revenue, immunity to the US-China trade war as an Israeli company, exposure to 5G, and potential integration into Apple's future iPhones. The increased valuation reflects the anticipated growth in the semiconductor IP market and a shift towards chiplet models.

title: TSMC To Mass Produce Breakthrough 2nm MBCFET Transistors In 2024
summary: TSMC has achieved a breakthrough in its research and development for the 2nm semiconductor manufacturing node, with plans for trial production in mid-2023 and mass production in 2024. The 2nm process will utilize a new Multi-Bridge Channel Field Effect (MBCFET) transistor design, an evolution over the current FinFET designs and similar to Samsung's approach for its 3nm process. If the projected 90% yield rate for the 2nm process is achieved by 2023, it positions TSMC for a smooth transition to volume production.

title: Skytrac To Make Iridium Certus Terminals
summary: Skytrac Systems is developing new Iridium satcom products, specifically Iridium Certus terminals, designed to support bandwidth-intensive services such as video streaming. The company's SDL-350 Iridium Certus terminal is highlighted as a key product in this new line. This move aims to enhance capabilities for aviation communications.

title: VMware Embraces Nvidia GPUs, DPUs To Drive Enterprise AI
summary: VMware has partnered with Nvidia to integrate GPUs and data processing units (DPUs) into its cloud offerings, aiming to make AI more accessible and easier for enterprises to adopt. The collaboration involves integrating Nvidia's NGC software suite into VMware's virtualization platforms and a broader "Project Monterey" to re-architect VMware's Cloud Foundation with SmartNICs for modern workloads. This initiative seeks to simplify AI deployment, improve performance, and enhance security by making GPUs first-class compute citizens within the VMware ecosystem.

title: Intel Spins Out Omni-Path Interconnect Business Into Stand-Alone Company
summary: Intel has spun out its Omni-Path Architecture high-speed interconnect technology into a new stand-alone company called Cornelis Networks, which has raised $20 million in Series A funding. This move provides an alternative to Nvidia's Mellanox InfiniBand and allows former Intel architects to continue developing and supporting the Omni-Path product line, which Intel had previously de-emphasized. Cornelis Networks aims to support existing customers, sell current products, and develop next-generation interconnect solutions for high-performance computing and AI workloads.

title: NVIDIA Announces Cloud-AI Video-Streaming Platform to Better Connect Millions Working and Studying Remotely
summary: NVIDIA has launched Maxine, a cloud-AI video-streaming platform designed to enhance video conferencing for millions working and studying remotely. This GPU-accelerated platform enables service providers to offer AI-powered features like super resolution, gaze correction, and noise cancellation, while significantly reducing bandwidth consumption. It leverages cloud-native architecture for scalability and integrates NVIDIA's AI SDKs to improve video and audio quality, making virtual interactions more engaging and efficient.

title: Nvidia Offers UK Covid Supercomputer While Waiting on Arm Deal
summary: Nvidia is building a $50 million supercomputer, "Cambridge-1," in the UK to aid COVID-19 healthcare research, offering 400 petaflops of AI computing power to institutions like GlaxoSmithKline and King's College London. This initiative comes as Nvidia awaits government approval for its $40 billion acquisition of British tech company Arm, with regulators scrutinizing potential conditions on job retention in the UK. The supercomputer is described as a non-commercial endeavor to provide much-needed computing resources for researchers.

title: NVIDIA Building UK’s Most Powerful Supercomputer, Dedicated to AI Research in Healthcare
summary: NVIDIA announced it is building Cambridge-1, the UK's most powerful supercomputer, which will be dedicated to AI research in healthcare, including tackling COVID-19. Pharmaceutical companies like GSK and AstraZeneca, along with King's College London and Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, will utilize the system. Cambridge-1 will provide 400 petaflops of AI performance and will be part of an NVIDIA AI Center of Excellence in Cambridge.

title: With SuperPod, Nvidia makes supercomputing a bigger focus of its AI strategy
summary: Nvidia introduced new AI technologies, including SuperPod Solution for Enterprise, which allows businesses to build supercomputers optimized for deep learning in weeks. SuperPod uses DGX A100 appliances and Mellanox networking to create powerful systems, with Nvidia announcing its own 400-petaflop SuperPod in the UK and another for India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The company also unveiled the Jetson Nano 2GB for AI development and education, and Maxine, a cloud-based AI service to reduce video call bandwidth.

title: New AI Technologies Announced at GTC 2020 Keynote
summary: During GTC 2020, NVIDIA unveiled significant updates, including new AI technologies focused on optimizing video streaming, conversational AI, and recommender systems. Key announcements included NVIDIA Maxine for cloud-native video AI, TensorRT 7.2 for accelerated deep learning inference, and the Riva Open Beta for building real-time conversational AI services. The company also introduced the NVIDIA Merlin Open Beta for end-to-end deep learning recommender system development.

title: What is a data processing unit, and why should you care?
summary: Data Processing Units (DPUs) are enhanced network interface cards (NICs) designed to offload infrastructure tasks from a server's central processing unit (CPU), thereby improving performance and extending server life. Nvidia recently introduced two DPU models, the BlueField-2 DPU and the BlueField-2X, with the latter incorporating Nvidia's Ampere GPUs for AI acceleration. The article argues that DPUs are well-timed for current data center needs, driven by high server utilization and the demands of AI, and benefit from strong ecosystem support from major players like VMware and Red Hat.

title: NVIDIA Introduces New Family of BlueField DPUs to Bring Breakthrough Networking, Storage and Security Performance to Every Data Center
summary: NVIDIA has announced a new family of Data Processing Units (DPUs) called BlueField, accompanied by the DOCA software development kit, to enhance networking, storage, and security performance in data centers. These DPUs offload critical tasks from CPUs, thereby freeing up processing power for other enterprise applications. Major server manufacturers and software partners like VMware, Red Hat, and Canonical are integrating NVIDIA DPUs into their offerings.

title: NVIDIA Announces Ready-Made NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs, Offered by Global Network of Certified Partners
summary: NVIDIA has announced the DGX SuperPOD Solution for Enterprise, a turnkey AI infrastructure allowing organizations to rapidly deploy powerful AI supercomputers. These systems range from 20 to 140 NVIDIA DGX A100 systems, offering 100 to 700 petaflops of AI performance, and are being adopted by leading organizations like NAVER, Linköping University, and C-DAC for advanced AI research and development. NVIDIA also noted plans to build Cambridge-1, the UK's fastest supercomputer, which will accelerate healthcare research.

title: Global Technology Leaders Adopt NVIDIA EGX Edge AI Platform to Infuse Intelligence at the Edge of Every Business
summary: NVIDIA announced the widespread adoption of its EGX edge AI platform by leading technology companies, enabling the deployment of secure, GPU-accelerated software and services at the edge across various industries. The platform now integrates NVIDIA Ampere architecture GPUs and BlueField-2 DPUs for enhanced security and performance. NVIDIA also introduced Fleet Command, a hybrid cloud platform for remote management of AI applications and models on edge servers, with early adopters including KION Group and Northwestern Memorial Hospital.

title: Supermicro to Support NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPU on Industry's Broadest Portfolio of Servers Optimized for Accelerated Computational Workloads in AI, AR/DR, and Data Analytics
summary: Supermicro announced its intent to support the new NVIDIA BlueField-2 DPU, with an aggressive certification program planned for 2021 across a broad range of its server systems. This initiative aims to enhance performance for accelerated workloads in AI, AR/DR, and data analytics by leveraging the DPU's capabilities to offload tasks from the CPU and boost security and efficiency. Supermicro plans to integrate the BlueField-2 DPU into various server products, from GPU systems to embedded solutions, highlighting its rapid time-to-market approach.

title: US tech giant Nvidia unveils ‘breakthrough’ processor sired by Israel team
summary: Nvidia Corp. unveiled a new "breakthrough" processor called the Data Processing Unit (DPU) developed by its Israeli team, Mellanox Technologies Ltd., which Nvidia acquired in 2019 for $7 billion. This DPU is designed to offload data center infrastructure services from the main CPU, significantly freeing up server resources and enhancing performance. Nvidia plans to integrate these DPUs into new server systems by 2021 and projects future versions to be significantly more powerful.

title: Semiconductor Market to reach USD 90.80 billion by 2024, Broadcom Inc. and Infineon Technologies AG emerge as Key Contributors to growth | Technavio
summary: The semiconductor market is projected to grow by USD 90.80 billion during 2020-2024, progressing at a CAGR of over 4%. This growth is significantly driven by the rising adoption of semiconductor ICs in automobiles and emerging semiconductor packaging technologies. Broadcom Inc. and Infineon Technologies AG, along with other major players, are identified as key contributors to this market expansion, with the APAC region expected to contribute 76% of the market growth.

title: NVIDIA Merlin Powers Fastest Commercially Available Solution for Recommender Systems Training
summary: NVIDIA Merlin, specifically HugeCTR combined with a single NVIDIA DGX A100 system, has been recognized as the fastest commercially available solution for training recommender systems. This achievement was demonstrated in the MLPerf v0.07 benchmark, where it significantly outperformed a 16 CPU cluster by training a Deep Learning Recommender Model network 13.5 times faster. The rapid training speed of 3.33 minutes highlights NVIDIA's commitment to advancing large-scale deep learning recommenders, enabling quicker iteration and experimentation in machine learning workflows.

title: Samsung beats TSMC to win new Qualcomm order to make mobile chips
summary: Samsung Electronics has secured a deal with Qualcomm to manufacture 5G-capable mobile application processors, specifically the Snapdragon 750 chips, using its 8 nanometer technology. This agreement, along with a recent 1 trillion won deal for Snapdragon 875 chips using 5 nm technology, signifies Samsung's growing prowess in the foundry business and its competitive edge against market leader TSMC. The company is investing heavily in foundry technology and packaging processes to narrow the gap with TSMC and is expected to increase its share of the global foundry market.

title: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses AI, data centers, getting acquired by Nvidia and more
summary: Arm CEO Simon Segars discusses the 2020 acquisition by Nvidia for $40 billion, highlighting the strategic alignment of both companies in AI and data centers. He emphasizes that the merger will accelerate Arm's trajectory into new markets like automotive and data centers, while also expanding their IP offerings. Segars addresses regulatory hurdles and concerns about licensing to Chinese companies, asserting that the deal is pro-competitive and will not alter Arm's licensing approach.

title: AMD’s Xilinx Acquisition Offer Likely To Be Rejected Believe Analysts
summary: Analysts are skeptical about AMD's proposed acquisition of Xilinx for up to $20 billion, despite a 20% premium. Many believe there are insufficient synergies between the two companies or that Xilinx management will reject the offer due to their strong position in the programmable device market. AMD's likely motive is to compete with Intel in FPGAs, but benefits are seen as long-term.

title: HLAL Chart | Wahed FTSE USA Shariah ETF
summary: This page provides a live, interactive chart for the Wahed FTSE USA Shariah ETF (HLAL), displaying real-time data, price movements, and various technical analysis tools. Users can customize the chart type and apply indicators to understand price trends. The article also lists current financial market data, including major indices, commodities, and individual stock performances.

title: Arm co-founder: Nvidia takeover would create another US tech monopoly
summary: Hermann Hauser, co-founder of Arm, has warned that Nvidia's proposed $40bn takeover of the British chip designer would lead to the creation of another US tech monopoly, destroying Arm's "even-handed" business model. He urged the UK government to intervene to prevent the sale, suggesting that Arm instead be taken public on a major stock exchange with a golden share for the UK. Hauser also highlighted the national security implications and the importance of retaining a world-leading British tech company.

title: Samsung leader visits ASML
summary: Samsung Electronics Vice Chairman Lee Jae-yong visited ASML Holding N.V.'s headquarters in the Netherlands to view extreme ultraviolet (EUV) equipment. This equipment is critical for producing advanced chips (7-nanometer process or below). The visit highlights Samsung's focus on securing essential technology for its semiconductor manufacturing.

title: Samsung heir Lee Jae-Yong returns after meeting Dutch chipmaking equipment firm
summary: Samsung Vice Chairman Lee Jae-Yong has returned to South Korea after meeting with top officials from ASML Holding N.V. in the Netherlands. Discussions focused on the supply of critical chipmaking equipment, cooperation on advanced manufacturing technology, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the chip industry. Samsung aims to boost its competitiveness in the storage and logic chip segments, especially with the essential role of EUV lithography in advanced chip production.

title: CINECA to Build World’s Fastest AI Supercomputer with NVIDIA and Atos
summary: CINECA, an Italian inter-university consortium, announced a partnership with NVIDIA and Atos to build "Leonardo," the world's fastest AI supercomputer. This new system, featuring nearly 14,000 NVIDIA Ampere architecture-based GPUs, will deliver 10 exaflops of AI performance. Procured by EuroHPC, Leonardo aims to solidify Italy's leadership in AI and high-performance computing research, supporting advancements in drug discovery, space exploration, and weather modeling.

title: US firm Nvidia to employ 100 West Bank engineers as salaried workers
summary: Nvidia Corp., which acquired Israel’s Mellanox Technologies Ltd., will employ 100 Palestinian engineers in the West Bank as salaried workers, converting them from subcontractors. This move is hailed as a historic achievement for Palestinian workers, offering them new professional and personal opportunities within the US firm. Mellanox co-founder Eyal Waldman emphasized the positive impact of joint Israeli-Palestinian professional work and urged other companies to follow suit.

title: Opinion: How did Intel lose its Silicon Valley crown?
summary: This article discusses Intel's decline as the leading chip manufacturer in Silicon Valley, examining whether the challenges stem from technological limits or leadership decisions. The chip giant announced a delay in its 7-nanometer manufacturing process and considered outsourcing some production for a key next-generation chip, shocking investors and analysts. This move is seen as a significant setback for the company once considered the standard-bearer of Moore's Law.

title: Opinion: How did Intel lose its Silicon Valley crown?
summary: Intel, while still a dominant chip provider, has lost its status as Silicon Valley's chip king due to significant delays in its 7-nanometer manufacturing process and potential outsourcing of next-generation chip components. This situation has led to questions regarding whether technological limits, leadership decisions, or a combination of both are contributing to the company's struggles. The decision to potentially use a contract manufacturer for vital next-gen chips has been seen as a significant setback for a company long associated with Moore's Law.

title: Synopsys, Cadence, and Agnisys Release Major Platform Updates to EDA Tools
summary: Three major Electronic Design Automation (EDA) companies, Synopsys, Cadence, and Agnisys, have introduced significant updates to their software tools to enhance IC design. Synopsys launched its Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) platform for post-silicon analysis, while Cadence released System-Level Verification IP (VIP) to improve SoC testbench assembly and verification efficiency. Agnisys introduced SLIP-G and SoC Enterprise to assist with IP generation and SoC design assembly respectively.

title: Intel Unveils Next-Gen SmartNICs As Nvidia Plots DPU Takeover
summary: Intel has launched new FPGA-based SmartNICs, including the Intel FPGA SmartNIC C5000X platform and the Silicom FPGA SmartNIC N5010, targeting cloud data centers and 5G networks. These products aim to enhance performance and reduce operating costs by offloading workloads from CPUs. The move positions Intel against rivals like Nvidia, which recently introduced its own DPUs, and potentially AMD, which is rumored to be acquiring Xilinx.

title: Adobe Photoshop Gets New NVIDIA AI-Powered Neural Filters That Can Automatically Age You
summary: Adobe Photoshop has introduced new AI-powered neural filters, developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, to enhance image editing. One notable feature is the Smart Portrait Filter, which utilizes NVIDIA StyleGAN2 technology to allow users to easily adjust facial characteristics like gaze, lighting, and age with simple sliders. This technology dramatically speeds up complex adjustments that would typically require extensive manual work.

title: Nvidia’s A100 GPU sets new performance records in MLPerf benchmarks
summary: Nvidia's A100 GPU has set new performance records in the latest MLPerf benchmarks, dominating tests across six application areas for data center and edge computing systems. The A100 GPU significantly outperformed CPUs in image classification and recommender tests, demonstrating extreme cost efficiency benefits for AI inference. Nvidia's systems are also making an impact in various industries, including medical imaging, automotive, and financial services, and are integrated into powerful supercomputers.

title: Huawei, China firms said to seek curbs on Nvidia’s arm deal
summary: Chinese technology companies, including Huawei, have expressed significant concerns to local regulators regarding Nvidia Corp.'s proposed $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. They fear Nvidia might force Arm to cut off Chinese clients, jeopardizing Arm's neutral status in the chip industry and impacting their access to crucial technology. The deal requires approval from various global regulators, with China's endorsement being particularly challenging due to its reliance on American technology and ongoing trade tensions.

title: Nvidia deal for Arm will drive computing power growth, says SoftBank’s CEO
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. CEO Masayoshi Son stated that the sale of chip designer Arm to Nvidia Corp. will boost computing power growth, marking his first public comments since the $40 billion deal announcement. Son made these remarks at an AI summit hosted by Saudi Arabia, emphasizing his belief in AI's societal transformation. The deal, part of SoftBank's asset sales, has raised concerns about Arm's neutrality as a supplier, but Son remains optimistic about its implications for future investment and AI acceleration.

title: Xilinx rockets 14% after finalizing agreement for $35 billion sale to AMD
summary: Xilinx shares jumped 14% after Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) agreed to acquire the company in a $35 billion all-stock deal, expected to close by the end of 2021. The acquisition aims to boost AMD's presence in communications technology and create operational efficiencies, making the combined entity a stronger competitor against Intel. Xilinx shareholders will receive 1.7234 shares of AMD for each Xilinx share they own.

title: Waymo, Daimler to partner in developing self-driving semi trucks
summary: Daimler AG's commercial truck unit and Alphabet Inc's Waymo announced a partnership to develop self-driving Class 8 semi trucks, integrating Waymo's automated system into Daimler's Freightliner Cascadia. This collaboration aims to accelerate the deployment of automated heavy-duty trucks, a market where several companies are competing to reduce reliance on human drivers. Despite the partnership, Daimler will continue its in-house development of robotic truck drivers, offering a dual-strategy approach for its customers.

title: AMD Agrees to Buy Xilinx for $35 Billion in Stock (Published 2020)
summary: Advanced Micro Devices has agreed to acquire Xilinx for $35 billion in an all-stock deal, aiming to expand its chip business into new markets like 5G communications and automotive electronics. This acquisition is part of a broader trend of consolidation in the chip industry and would position AMD to compete more fiercely with rivals like Nvidia and Intel. The deal is expected to help AMD grow its presence in data centers and enhance its profitability.

title: 8 Tech Stocks Of Tomorrow Investors Should Buy Today
summary: This article highlights eight tech stocks—Alibaba, Salesforce.com, DocuSign, Fastly, JD.Com, NVIDIA, Alarm.com, and Enphase Energy—that are poised for significant future growth. It explains how each company, despite some already being strong performers, has unique aspects or recent developments that position them as "tomorrow's next big thing" for investors. The article emphasizes specific growth drivers for each stock, such as market expansion, accelerated adoption due to recent trends, or pioneering new technologies.

title: Marvell Acquires Inphi For Cloud Push
summary: Marvell has announced its acquisition of Inphi for $10 billion, an all-cash-and-stock deal aimed at strengthening its position in cloud data centers and 5G technology. The acquisition is part of a broader consolidation trend in the chip sector, following other major deals like AMD's purchase of Xilinx and Nvidia's acquisition of ARM. Marvell plans to re-domicile in the United States, creating a "US semiconductor powerhouse" with an enterprise value of approximately $40 billion, leveraging Inphi's high-speed data interconnect platform for cloud infrastructure.

title: HP Announces New 3D Printing Software Powered by Dyndrite, New TPA Powder with Evonik
summary: HP has announced two significant developments in the 3D printing space: the launch of HP's Universal Build Manager Powered by Dyndrite and a new co-branded thermoplastic amide (TPA) elastomer developed with Evonik. The software, built on Dyndrite's Accelerated Geometry Engine, aims to enhance CAD-to-print workflows with automation and scalability, supporting various additive manufacturing technologies. The new TPA powder is optimized for HP's Multi Jet Fusion technology, offering high flexibility, fatigue resistance, and suitability for demanding functional parts in sectors like automotive and sporting goods.

title: Waldman to leave Mellanox two decades after founding unicorn
summary: Eyal Waldman, president and CEO of Mellanox Technologies Ltd., announced his departure from the company he founded in 1999. His exit follows last year's $6.9 billion sale of Mellanox to Nvidia Corp., a deal that rewarded Waldman approximately $250 million for his 3.6% stake. Waldman led Mellanox to a Nasdaq IPO in 2007 and is recognized as a prominent Israeli tech entrepreneur.

title: Origin PC's NS-15 Workstation Laptop Is Ryzen 9 5950X Ready
summary: Origin PC announced its NS-15 workstation laptop would support AMD's new Ryzen 5000-series desktop CPUs, including the flagship Ryzen 9 5950X, despite a later correction clarifying this was an error. The laptop is designed with a thick chassis for cooling, allowing for desktop-class performance in a portable, albeit heavy, form factor. Pricing varies significantly by configuration, but a high-end build with a Ryzen 9 5950X, 32GB RAM, and an RTX 2070 Max-P was estimated at around $3100.

title: NVIDIA Names Aarti Shah to Board of Directors
summary: NVIDIA announced the appointment of Aarti Shah, Senior Vice President and Chief Information and Digital Officer of Eli Lilly and Company, to its board of directors. Shah, a leader in IT, digital health, cybersecurity, and data sciences, brings extensive experience at the intersection of computer science and healthcare. This marks the second board appointment for NVIDIA in 2020, expanding the board to 13 members.

title: Hyundai Motor Group Selects NVIDIA DRIVE Infotainment and AI Platform for All Future Hyundai, Kia and Genesis Models
summary: Hyundai Motor Group has selected the NVIDIA DRIVE in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) and AI platform to be standard across all its future Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis models starting in 2022. This integration will provide a software-defined AI user experience that is perpetually updateable, allowing for new functionalities and enhanced safety features post-purchase. The NVIDIA DRIVE platform will enable Hyundai Motor Group to roll out its new connected car operating system (ccOS), enhancing connectivity and offering integrated services to drivers and occupants.

title: Micron Ships World's First 176-Layer NAND With Huge Gains In Performance And Storage Density
summary: Micron has announced the shipment of the world's first 176-layer 3D NAND flash memory, marking a significant advancement in storage technology. This new generation of NAND offers over 35% improvements in read and write latency, a 30% smaller die size, and data rates up to 1,600 MT/s. Micron plans to integrate this technology across a wide range of devices, from smartphones and consoles to SSDs for client and data center applications, while also transitioning to 3D replacement-gate NAND for future enhancements in power efficiency, performance, and capacity.

title: Apple's new Macs could revive the PC chip wars, analysts say
summary: Apple's expected unveiling of new Mac computers with in-house processor chips based on Arm Ltd. technology could re-ignite competition in the PC chip market, currently dominated by Intel and Advanced Micro Devices. This shift marks a departure from Apple's nearly 15-year relationship with Intel and could benefit companies like Qualcomm, which has been adapting Arm-based processors for Windows PCs. Analysts believe Apple's entry will accelerate the adoption of Arm-based PCs, although challenges remain for software compatibility.

title: Apple's new Macs could revive the PC chip wars, benefit Qualcomm: Analysts
summary: Apple is expected to unveil new Mac computers using its own in-house Arm-based processor chips, a move that could disrupt the PC chip market currently dominated by Intel and AMD. This shift could benefit companies like Qualcomm, which has been developing Arm-based processors for Windows PCs. Analysts suggest that Apple's entry into this market could accelerate the adoption of Arm-based PCs, despite challenges related to software compatibility.

title: Chip maker NVIDIA signs in-car entertainment system deal with Hyundai Motor
summary: NVIDIA Corp announced a deal with Hyundai Motor Group to integrate its NVIDIA DRIVE in-vehicle information and entertainment system into all Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis models starting in 2022. This system, which includes hardware and perpetually updatable AI software, is already in use in some Genesis models. NVIDIA declined to provide specific vehicle numbers but noted that Hyundai Motor Group shipped over 7 million vehicles in 2019, indicating a large-scale implementation.

title: Hyundai Motor to install Nvidia’s in-vehicle system in entire fleet from 2022
summary: Hyundai Motor Group announced it will integrate Nvidia's Drive connected car platform into all its Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis models starting in 2022. This partnership aims to enhance the in-vehicle information and entertainment system with perpetual software updates and AI features. The collaboration builds on existing work between the two companies, with Hyundai Motor Group chairman Chung Euisun pushing for a transformation into a future mobility solutions provider.

title: Synopsys acquires Moortec as Silicon LifeCycle Management is New Mantra
summary: Synopsys has announced the acquisition of UK-based Moortec, a company specializing in in-chip monitoring technology. This acquisition is part of Synopsys' strategy to enhance its silicon lifecycle management (SLM) platform, leveraging Moortec's process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensors to improve chip design, manufacturing, and in-field operation. The move is aimed at addressing the increasing complexity of SoCs and the need for data-analytics-driven optimization across the semiconductor lifecycle.

title: TSMC sets up Arizona, USA subsidiary with $3.5 billion in capital
summary: TSMC announced its board approved a $3.5 billion investment to establish a wholly-owned subsidiary in Arizona, USA, for a new chip manufacturing plant. This move supports the Trump administration's goal of bringing tech supply chains to the US and follows TSMC's earlier plans for a $12 billion factory in the state. The plant is expected to begin construction in 2021 and produce chips by 2024.

title: Corsair's Vengeance A7200 Is A Gaming PC Powerhouse With Ryzen 9 5900X And GeForce RTX 3080 Credentials
summary: Corsair has introduced its new Vengeance a7200 Series Gaming PC, offering configurations with AMD's Ryzen 9 5900X processor and NVIDIA's GeForce RTX 3080 graphics card. This pre-built system provides a solution for gamers struggling to acquire these in-demand components separately. The PCs feature Corsair's own branded components and come with a two-year warranty.

title: Amazon shifts some voice assistant, face recognition computing to its own chips
summary: Amazon is transitioning some of the computing for its Alexa voice assistant and Rekognition facial recognition service to its custom-designed "Inferentia" chips. This strategic move aims to improve speed and reduce costs by moving away from third-party chip providers like Nvidia. The company reports a 25% improvement in latency and 30% lower costs for Alexa's text-to-speech tasks with the new chips.

title: Corsair's new gaming PC has all the hardware you can't buy right now
summary: Corsair has launched its new Vengeance a7200 gaming PC, featuring hard-to-find components like AMD Ryzen 5000 series CPUs and Nvidia GeForce RTX 30 series GPUs. While these parts are scarce for DIY builders, prebuilt systems offer a way to acquire them. However, even Corsair faces supply limitations, with only specific configurations currently available for purchase.

title: Why Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are all building AI notetakers for doctors
summary: Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are developing AI-powered notetaking tools for doctors to address the time-consuming and often inaccurate process of medical transcription. These tools aim to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recording patient interactions and medical records, moving beyond existing methods that doctors find cumbersome or overly generalized. While some solutions are already available, tech giants are focusing on delivering more precise and sophisticated AI to streamline healthcare documentation.

title: Alternatives for Uncertain Times: VanEck's SMH ETF
summary: The VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is positioned for continued growth, especially with a potential easing of US-China trade tensions under a new administration. Analyst forecasts suggest that improved trade relations would benefit semiconductor companies by expanding market access and alleviating supply chain issues. The industry has also become more efficient, making SMH an attractive growth play amidst increasing global demand for chips.

title: Nvidia doubles the memory of its A100 GPU for AI workloads
summary: Nvidia has announced an updated version of its A100 GPU, doubling its memory to 80GB, which significantly enhances its performance for AI workloads and large datasets. This new GPU, capable of delivering over 2 terabytes per second of memory bandwidth, is integrated into the existing Nvidia DGX A100 system and the new DGX Station A100 workgroup server. Additionally, Nvidia is boosting its Mellanox InfiniBand networking technology to 400 gigabits per second, further accelerating AI and HPC applications.

title: NVIDIA Announces Mellanox InfiniBand for Exascale AI Supercomputing
summary: NVIDIA is introducing the next generation of NVIDIA Mellanox 400G InfiniBand, offering faster networking performance for AI developers and scientific researchers. This new technology provides ultra-low latency, double data throughput, and new In-Network Computing engines for enhanced acceleration, vital for fields like drug discovery and climate research. Leading infrastructure manufacturers and storage partners are integrating this technology into their solutions, aiming to tackle the most challenging computing problems with unmatched performance and efficiency.

title: NVIDIA Doubles Down: Announces A100 80GB GPU, Supercharging World’s Most Powerful GPU for AI Supercomputing
summary: NVIDIA has announced the A100 80GB GPU, an enhancement to its AI supercomputing platform, doubling the memory of its predecessor to 80GB and delivering over 2 terabytes per second of memory bandwidth. This new GPU offers unprecedented speed and performance for AI and scientific research, enabling faster acceleration of applications and the ability to handle larger models and datasets. Leading system providers are set to integrate the A100 80GB into their systems, supporting diverse data-intensive applications from AI training and inferencing to big data analytics and scientific simulations.

title: NVIDIA DGX Station A100 Offers Researchers AI Data-Center-in-a-Box
summary: NVIDIA has announced the DGX Station A100, a petascale workgroup server designed to bring AI capabilities out of data centers and into offices and labs. This second-generation AI system features four NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPUs with up to 320GB of GPU memory, offering 2.5 petaflops of AI performance. It also supports NVIDIA's multi-instance GPU (MIG) technology, providing up to 28 separate GPU instances to support parallel jobs and multiple users.

title: Nvidia beats on both earnings and revenue, sales up 57%
summary: Nvidia reported earnings for its fiscal third quarter of 2021, exceeding analyst expectations for both earnings per share ($2.91 vs $2.57) and revenue ($4.73 billion vs $4.41 billion). The company achieved record revenue, up 57% year-over-year, driven by its compute and networking segment and strong gaming sales. Despite the positive results, the stock dropped in extended trading due to a projected sequential decline in data center revenue for the upcoming quarter.

title: RBC and Borealis AI announce new AI private cloud platform
summary: RBC and its AI research institute Borealis AI have partnered with NVIDIA and Red Hat to create a new AI private cloud platform. This infrastructure provides Borealis AI's researchers with high-performance computing resources to develop machine learning applications, ultimately transforming the customer banking experience. The platform, powered by Red Hat OpenShift and NVIDIA’s DGX AI computing systems, is designed to efficiently handle both research and production workloads, accelerating financial analysis and improving trading execution.

title: NVIDIA Earns Record $4.7 Billion Revenue In Q3 2021 Aided By Nintendo Switch, Lockdowns
summary: NVIDIA reported a record $4.7 billion in revenue for Q3 fiscal year 2021, exceeding guidance and analyst estimates. This 57% year-over-year growth was primarily driven by strong performance in its gaming and data center segments. The Nintendo Switch and COVID-19-related lockdowns significantly contributed to the gaming revenue boom, while the acquisition of Mellanox boosted data center sales.

title: U.S. upgrades safety probe into nearly 159,000 Tesla vehicles
summary: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has expanded its safety probe into approximately 159,000 Tesla Model S and Model X vehicles, upgrading it to an engineering analysis. This investigation concerns touchscreen failures that can lead to loss of rear-camera display, impact defogging, and affect driver assistance system chimes. NHTSA reported that failure rates exceeded 30% in some vehicles, prompting Tesla to issue over-the-air updates to mitigate the issues.

title: Earnings: Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) reports Q3 2021 financial results
summary: Nvidia reported a sharp increase in third-quarter earnings for 2021, surpassing market projections. Adjusted profit climbed to $2.91 per share, and revenue rose 57% annually to $4.73 billion, both exceeding Street views. Despite strong results, the company's stock dropped during after-hours trading following the announcement.

title: Modern Networks For An Increasingly Distributed IT World
summary: This article discusses how companies like VMware are developing "modern networks" to address the challenges of an increasingly distributed IT world, amplified by factors like cloud adoption, edge computing, and remote work. VMware's strategy centers on its NSX software-defined networking platform, Project Monterey, and leveraging SmartNICs to offload virtualization and security functions, aiming for automated, cloud-like network scenarios. The goal is to provide secure, low-latency access to applications from anywhere, with features like enhanced firewalls, services mesh, and Kubernetes networking solutions.

title: Nvidia, Epic to bring 'Fortnite' back to iPhones in 'near future'
summary: Nvidia and Epic Games are collaborating to bring "Fortnite" back to Apple iPhones through Nvidia's GeForce NOW streaming game service in the near future. The game was removed from Apple's App Store in August due to Epic's billing system, which violated Apple's rules. This return route bypasses Apple's App Store rules by utilizing the iPhone's Safari web browser.

title: Why Some Exposure to VanEck’s Gaming ETF Is Prudent
summary: The article discusses the growth and mainstream adoption of the esports industry, highlighting its global phenomenon status and substantial investment from various sectors beyond just tech. It suggests that the VanEck Vectors Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO) is a prudent investment for those seeking exposure to the gaming and related industries, including major players like Tencent and Activision Blizzard, as well as chipmakers like NVIDIA and AMD. The ETF is presented as a way to capitalize on the continued surge in the gaming and esports market.

title: NVIDIA Broadens Product Portfolio to Tap New Computing Markets
summary: NVIDIA has seen exponential growth in recent years, driven by its strategy of leveraging a single GPU architecture across diverse applications and increasing its average selling price. The company is now expanding its product portfolio into new markets, such as AI, by investing more in software and exploring new verticals. Despite short-term challenges, NVIDIA's long-term growth prospects are strong as it broadens its addressable market.

title: NVIDIA Unlikely to Compete with AMD on 7-nm Node
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is developing ray tracing technology for its future GPUs, with plans to launch 7-nm gaming GPUs ahead of NVIDIA. NVIDIA, however, is not rushing to adopt 7-nm technology, focusing instead on affordable and power-efficient 12-nm FinFET processes for its current Turing GPUs. The article suggests NVIDIA might skip 7-nm and directly move to 7-nm+ or 5-nm nodes in the future.

title: Why Teradyne’s offerings provide value to end-user markets
summary: This article examines Teradyne's (TER) diverse product line and how it delivers value to its customer base across various end-user markets. It details Teradyne's semiconductor test platforms like FLEX, J750, and Magnum, and how they cater to industries such as mobile, automotive, and data storage. The article also highlights Teradyne's key customers and its presence in semiconductor-focused ETFs.

title: UCI, UCLA and UC Berkeley team up to organize esports holiday tournament
summary: UCI, UCLA, and UC Berkeley esports programs are collaborating to pilot a UC Esports Initiative, starting with a holiday tournament for all nine UC undergraduate campuses. The event aims to boost student engagement and foster community during remote instruction, featuring games like League of Legends, Overwatch, and Valorant, along with community events. Sponsored by Xfinity, CORSAIR, and MSI, the tournament will offer prizes including scholarships and will be streamed on a new UC esports Twitch channel.

title: Global Semiconductor Market (2020 to 2024) - Industry Trends, Share, Size, Growth, Opportunity and Forecast | Technavio
summary: The semiconductor market is projected to grow by USD 90.80 billion between 2020 and 2024, exhibiting a CAGR of over 4%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing adoption of semiconductor ICs in automobiles and advancements in semiconductor packaging technology. Technavio's report offers a comprehensive analysis including market size, forecast, trends, and vendor analysis, covering the impact of COVID-19.

title: Famous Graphics Chips: Intel’s GPU History
summary: This article chronicles Intel's long and often challenging history in developing graphics processing units (GPUs) since 1983, leading up to its 2020 announcement of the Xe Max discrete GPU. It details five previous attempts at dGPUs and numerous integrated GPU developments. The author discusses Intel's ambition to create a scalable GPU architecture using technologies like EMIB and Foveros to span from entry-level notebooks to supercomputers.

title: Do These 5 AI Chip Startups Pose a Threat to Nvidia?
summary: This article examines five prominent AI chip startups—Graphcore, SambaNova, Cerebras Systems, Groq, and Tenstorrent—that are developing hardware to challenge Nvidia's dominance in the AI chip market. These companies aim to offer superior performance, lower power consumption, and reduced costs in data centers and edge computing. While Nvidia remains the market leader, these startups' rapid commercialization and technological advancements could lead to acquisitions or fiercer competition in the coming years.

title: How to Avoid Speed Bumps and Stay in the AI Fast Lane with Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure
summary: This article discusses the benefits of hybrid cloud infrastructure for AI development, combining the flexibility of cloud computing with the cost-effectiveness of on-premises systems. It highlights how NVIDIA DGX systems with Google Cloud's Anthos on bare metal can help organizations manage AI workloads efficiently, minimizing data gravity issues and supporting both rapid experimentation and scaling. The approach allows businesses to "own the base, rent the spike," ensuring continuous compute resource availability and optimal cost per training run.

title: NVIDIA acquires Swedish VCSEL startup
summary: NVIDIA has acquired OptiGOT, a Swedish tech startup specializing in high-performance VCSEL lasers. OptiGOT spun out of research at the Chalmers University of Technology and was corporatized through Chalmers Ventures. This acquisition follows NVIDIA's larger acquisition of ARM and positions the company in the rapidly growing VCSEL market.

title: NVIDIA Debuts GeForce RTX 3060 Family for the Holidays
summary: NVIDIA introduced the GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, the first GPU in the RTX 3060 family, priced at $399. Powered by the NVIDIA Ampere architecture, it offers performance faster than the RTX 2080 SUPER, with support for ray tracing and AI-powered DLSS, NVIDIA Reflex, and NVIDIA Broadcast. The new GPU will be available on December 2nd and aims to provide cutting-edge gaming experiences for the holiday season.

title: GeForce RTX 3060 Ti Out Now: Faster Than RTX 2080 SUPER, Starting At $399
summary: NVIDIA has launched the GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, the latest addition to its RTX 30 Series, priced at $399. This new GPU is touted as being faster than the RTX 2080 SUPER and significantly outperforms the RTX 2060 SUPER, offering exceptional performance for gaming, content creation, and productivity. It features NVIDIA's Ampere Architecture, including 2nd Gen Ray Tracing Cores, 3rd Gen Tensor Cores for AI, and supports technologies like DLSS, Reflex, and Broadcast.

title: Amazon's AWS To Leverage Israeli-Made AI Processors By Habana Labs
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) announced it will use Israeli AI processor developer Habana Labs' Gaudi accelerators. This move aims to reduce the cost of training AI datasets and lower operating expenses for customers, offering up to 40% better price-performance than current GPU-based EC2 instances for machine learning workloads. This development is seen as a significant challenge to Nvidia's dominance in the AI processing market.

title: Arm CEO expects regulators to ‘take a good look’ at the Nvidia deal
summary: Arm CEO Simon Segars anticipates regulatory bodies will thoroughly review Nvidia's proposed $40 billion acquisition of the British chip designer. The deal, announced in September, faces hurdles including obtaining approvals from various global jurisdictions and concerns from Chinese regulators and some British entrepreneurs. Segars emphasized that Arm's ability to provide technology globally would not change with the ownership, but acknowledged the complex regulatory process.

title: Latest Update to Isaac SDK is Available for Download
summary: NVIDIA has released Isaac SDK 2020.2, an update that brings crucial tools for robot development and intralogistics applications. This update features new Isaac GEMs for robot manipulation and navigation, alongside a "Factory-of-the-Future" intralogistics application with configurable support for navigation robots and robot arms in Isaac Sim. It also includes support for the NVIDIA Jetbot robot and an expanded ecosystem with driver support for industrial devices from partners like Framos Technologies, LIPS Corp, SICK, and Universal Robot.

title: NAND competition heats up as SK Hynix unveils 176-layer flash memory
summary: SK Hynix has developed 176-layer NAND flash memory, making it the industry's highest-density chip, following Micron Technology. This new chip improves cell read latency by 20% and data transfer speeds by 33%, enhancing cost competitiveness and productivity. The move intensifies competition in the NAND market, with Samsung also planning significant investments, as demand for NAND memory chips rises due to global shifts towards working from home.

title: Uber sells ATG self-driving business to Aurora at $4 billion
summary: Uber Technologies Inc is selling its autonomous driving unit, Uber Advanced Technologies Group (ATG), to self-driving car startup Aurora in an equity deal valued at $4 billion. Uber will also invest $400 million in Aurora, giving it approximately 26% ownership, with the aim to accelerate Uber's path to profitability by the end of 2021. This sale marks a significant drop in ATG's valuation from its previous $7.25 billion.

title: Talk Stars: Israeli AI Startup Brings Fluency to Natural Language Understanding
summary: Onvego, an Israeli startup and NVIDIA Inception member, is enhancing natural language understanding in AI-powered conversational interfaces, moving beyond keyword limitations to understand natural speech. Their technology, already used in Israel's toll road and emergency services, aims for wider application in devices like coffee machines and elevators, and especially in call centers using NVIDIA GPUs. The company is also working on a standalone container for edge devices, leveraging NVIDIA's support to expand its reach.

title: Intel, Nvidia probed over tech allegedly used against Uighurs
summary: Two US legislators, Senator Marco Rubio and Representative Jim McGovern, have sent letters to Intel Corp and Nvidia Corp, probing the sale of advanced computer chips allegedly used by China for mass surveillance on Uighurs in the Xinjiang region. The letters sought information on the companies' exports to China and whether they ensured their technology was not used for human rights abuses. Both companies have responded, with Intel stating it does not tolerate human rights violations and Nvidia declining to comment.

title: McGovern, Rubio Ask CEOs of Intel and NVIDIA About Possible Involvement in Human Rights Abuses in Xinjiang
summary: Representative James P. McGovern (D-MA) and Senator Marco Rubio (R-FL) sent letters to the CEOs of Intel Corporation and NVIDIA. They are seeking information regarding the sale of advanced computer chips that might be powering a supercomputer used by People's Republic of China (PRC) security forces. The concern is that these chips could be contributing to mass surveillance and human rights abuses against Uyghurs and other minorities in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR).

title: RISC-V And Marvell Technologies Advances Enable Storage Solutions
summary: The article discusses how RISC-V computing and Marvell Technologies' advancements are driving innovation in storage solutions. It highlights presentations from the 2020 RISC-V Summit, detailing Western Digital's and Seagate's utilization of RISC-V processors for their storage devices, including customized SSDs and enhanced HDD control. Marvell's contributions, such as Data Processor Units (DPUs), NVMe over Fabric support, Ethernet Bunch of Flash, and solutions for next-gen HDDs, are also explored, emphasizing their role in advancing data center, automotive, and edge storage.

title: Corsair Launches Hydro-X Series XG7 GPU Water Blocks
summary: Corsair has launched its new Hydro-X Series XG7 GPU water blocks, designed for NVIDIA's 30 series graphics cards, including Founders Edition, ASUS ROG STRIX, and MSI VENTUS models. These water blocks aim to provide superior cooling performance and enhanced aesthetics with RGB lighting for enthusiasts. They feature a full conversion design to cool the GPU, memory, and VRMs, and are available immediately.

title: Sustainable and Attainable: Zoox Unveils Autonomous Robotaxi Powered by NVIDIA
summary: Zoox has unveiled its purpose-built autonomous robotaxi, powered by NVIDIA technology, designed for urban mobility. The vehicle is a level 5 robotaxi featuring bi-directional capabilities, aiming to transform transportation by making it safer and more efficient. This collaboration between Zoox and NVIDIA, which began in 2017, highlights the potential for widespread adoption of robotaxis, potentially reducing car ownership and travel costs in urban areas.

title: Samsung clinches 2nd deal to make Nvidia’s latest gaming chips
summary: Samsung Electronics has secured a second deal this year to manufacture Nvidia's next-generation gaming GPUs, the Ampere GeForce RTX30 series, using its 8-nanometer process technology. This contract is significant as Samsung aims to narrow the gap with industry leader TSMC in the global foundry market, investing heavily in technology like EUV lithography and expanding its production capabilities. The deal for Nvidia's popular RTX3080 chip highlights Samsung's growing presence amid high demand and fierce competition.

title: Training a Text2Sparql Model with MK-SQuIT and NeMo | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: This article discusses an alternative approach to question answering (QA) using knowledge graphs and a neural machine translation model. It introduces MK-SQuIT, an open-source framework for generating synthetic English to SPARQL query pairs, which addresses the challenges of creating large, high-quality training datasets. The authors also demonstrate how NVIDIA's NeMo can be used to fine-tune a Text2Sparql model for this translation task, enabling efficient QA over knowledge graphs.

title: Element AI sold for $230-million as founders saw value mostly wiped out, document reveals
summary: Montreal startup Element AI Inc. was sold to ServiceNow Inc. for US$230-million, a deal that saw the value of common shares held by founders and many employees largely wiped out due to the company's financial struggles and inability to meet product development goals. While institutional shareholders are expected to recoup investments, the sale highlights the challenges faced by the highly hyped AI firm despite significant venture capital and government funding. The transaction involves ServiceNow retaining Element AI's research scientists and patents, effectively abandoning its business.

title: Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF FTEC
summary: This article provides an overview of the Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ETF (FTEC), detailing its current price, key metrics, and how to purchase it on eToro. The ETF aims to replicate the performance of the MSCI USA IMI Information Technology Index, focusing primarily on US-based IT companies like Apple, Microsoft, and NVIDIA. It highlights the ETF's investment strategy, top holdings, and historical performance data.

title: Dogwood Therapeutics Inc Stock Price Today | NASDAQ: DWTX Live
summary: This article provides live stock price data for Dogwood Therapeutics Inc. (NASDAQ: DWTX), including its current price ($2.980), daily range, 52-week range, and key financial statistics. It also highlights analyst ratings, company health assessments, and recent news related to the company's drug development and financial activities. The company, formerly Virios Therapeutics, Inc., focuses on developing medicines for pain and fatigue-related disorders.

title: Isaac Gym is NVIDIA’s reinforcement learning accelerator for robotics
summary: NVIDIA announced the preview release of Isaac Gym, a new physics simulation environment designed to accelerate reinforcement learning for AI and robotics research. This GPU-accelerated platform allows researchers to train complex RL tasks, previously requiring thousands of CPU cores, on a single GPU significantly faster and more efficiently. Isaac Gym leverages NVIDIA's PhysX engine and offers an end-to-end GPU RL pipeline, making advanced robotics research more accessible.

title: Is Caterpillar Stock Worth Buying for 2021?
summary: Caterpillar's stock is considered a potential buy for 2021 due to its cyclical recovery pattern, where it typically performs well after economic downturns. While the dividend is secure and the company aims to reduce cyclicality through increased services revenue, its current valuation is high, and the strength of the recovery in some key segments like mining and oil & gas remains uncertain. Investors focused on dividends might find it appealing, but others are advised to monitor capital spending in key industries before buying.

title: Nvidia rival Graphcore raises $222 million for AI chips with potential IPO on the horizon
summary: Graphcore, a U.K.-based chipmaker, has raised $222 million in a Series E funding round, valuing the company at $2.77 billion. This investment aims to fuel its global expansion and accelerate the development of its AI-specific intelligence processing units (IPUs) to compete with rivals like Nvidia and Intel. With total investment now at $710 million, CEO Nigel Toon has previously expressed interest in a potential public listing in the future.

title: SAP SE's (SAP) Subsidiary Qualtrics Set to Go Public in 2021
summary: SAP SE's subsidiary, Qualtrics, is planning an initial public offering (IPO) in 2021, with its shares to be listed on Nasdaq under the symbol "XM" at an estimated price range of $20-$24. SAP America will hold all of Qualtrics' Class B common shares post-IPO. The IPO aims to provide Qualtrics with greater autonomy to expand in the SaaS-based experience management software market, following its acquisition by SAP in 2019.

title: Speaker Spotlight: "staying on top of trends involves being a gamer yourself" says Roundhill Investments' Mario Stefanidis
summary: Mario Stefanidis of Roundhill Investments discusses the intersection of finance and the games industry, emphasizing the importance of being an active gamer to understand evolving trends. He highlights how the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated growth in gaming and predicts future trends like cloud gaming expansion and new VR titles. Stefanidis also shares insights into Roundhill Investments' focus on thematic investing in digital media and entertainment.

title: Covid-19 Supercharged 2020's Tech Winners. What About 2021?
summary: The pandemic significantly boosted tech companies like Zoom, Shopify, and Nvidia in 2020, as they capitalized on trends such as remote work, cloud computing, video gaming, and e-commerce. While these companies saw massive gains, the article questions whether these trends will continue to drive growth as the virus recedes in 2021. The shift to cloud computing, in particular, was accelerated by shelter-in-place orders, with Zoom becoming an essential tool for virtualized offices.
